title: Senior Accountant, Capital Markets
description:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

At Coinbase, our mission is to increase economic freedom in the world. To achieve this, we are building the most trusted and comprehensive platform for institutions to participate in the crypto economy. We are seeking a very specific candidate: someone who is passionate about our mission, relishes the pressure of solving the industry's hardest problems, and actively seeks feedback to operate as part of a championship team.

As a Senior Accountant on the Capital Markets Accounting team within Finance, you'll play a critical role in supporting Coinbase's expanding capital markets businesses. You'll own the accounting and regulatory reporting for our registered Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) and Broker-Dealer entities, helping ensure financial integrity, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence as we continue to scale.
This is a highly visible role that partners across Accounting, Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, and Compliance to launch new products, strengthen controls, and support a rapidly evolving business at the forefront of digital assets.


What you'll do

  • Own the monthly close for Coinbase's FCM and Broker-Dealer entities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, financial statement preparation, and quarterly and annual reporting.
  • Prepare and submit regulatory filings to the CFTC, NFA, and other applicable regulators, ensuring accuracy and timely execution of daily, monthly, and annual reporting requirements.
  • Lead internal and external audits for the FCM and Broker-Dealer entities, coordinating cross-functional stakeholders and driving successful audit outcomes.
  • Design, execute, and enhance internal controls over accounting, regulatory reporting, and compliance processes.
  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, and Compliance to support new product launches and evolving business initiatives, ensuring accounting and regulatory readiness from day one.
  • Monitor regulatory capital and liquidity requirements, proactively identifying and escalating risks while helping strengthen operational processes.
  • Identify opportunities to improve accounting operations through automation, scalable processes, and thoughtful use of technology.
What we're looking for
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or a related field with an active CPA license.
  • 5–7 years of experience in public accounting (Big Four preferred) and/or industry experience supporting Broker-Dealer, FCM, or other regulated financial services organizations.
  • Experience with regulatory reporting, financial close, audits, and internal controls within a regulated environment.
  • Knowledge of FINRA/SEC Broker-Dealer regulations, CFTC/NFA requirements for registered FCMs, and accounting guidance including ASC 815 (Derivatives and Hedging) and 17 CFR 1.20.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
  • Availability to work Eastern Time hours to support daily regulatory filing deadlines.
  • Experience using generative AI responsibly to improve workflow efficiency while maintaining appropriate human oversight and high-quality outputs.

  • Demonstrated experience leading multi-stakeholder initiatives from ideation through completion, ensuring strategic initiatives are managed and driving forward.
  • Advanced proficiency in G-Suite/Microsoft Office (expert-level slide building) and project management platforms, with a disciplined approach to documentation and digital organization..

title: Senior Director, Enterprise Risk Strategy
description:
Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without any hidden fees or compounding interest.

Affirm's Enterprise Risk team helps the company make better business decisions by bringing an enterprise-wide view of the risks that matter most. This isn't a traditional Enterprise Risk role focused on maintaining frameworks—it's about helping leaders navigate ambiguity, align on complex decisions, and make thoughtful tradeoffs as Affirm continues to scale.

As our Senior Director, Enterprise Risk, you'll partner closely with leaders across Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, and Credit Risk to solve high-impact business challenges where there isn't always a predefined playbook. Success in this role comes from exceptional business judgment, influence, curiosity, and the ability to simplify complexity—not simply operating traditional ERM programs.

If you're energized by solving hard problems, influencing executive decision-making, and building something different, we'd love to meet you!


What You’ll Do

  • Partner with executive leaders to navigate complex strategic, operational, product, and regulatory decisions while helping build alignment across differing perspectives.
  • Evolve Enterprise Risk into a trusted business partner by developing practical, scalable approaches that improve decision-making without adding unnecessary process.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships and influence senior stakeholders through thoughtful challenge, clear communication, and sound business judgment.
  • Lead enterprise-wide initiatives that help Affirm identify, assess, and respond to emerging risks across new products, technologies, and strategic priorities.
  • Strengthen Enterprise Risk capabilities—including operational risk, governance, third-party risk, business continuity, and executive reporting—to ensure they remain practical, scalable, and business-focused.
  • Lead and develop a lean, high-impact team, fostering a culture of curiosity, collaboration, and thoughtful execution.


What We Look For

  • 12+ years of experience in a regulated or risk-intensive environment such as fintech, financial services, or technology.
  • Experience leading business transformation, strategy, product risk, operations, governance, Chief of Staff, Enterprise Risk, or similar cross-functional initiatives
  • Exceptional business judgment with the ability to simplify complex problems and influence senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to build trust, challenge constructively, and drive alignment without formal authority or operating as a control function.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity, building new capabilities, and partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and other business-facing teams

A Note to Candidates

You don't need to have spent your entire career in Enterprise Risk to be successful in this role. If you've helped organizations navigate complex decisions, lead transformation, or influence executive teams in a regulated environment, we'd love to hear from you!

Equity Grade - USA 15

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)

USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $253,000 - $323,000

title: Internal Audit Data Analytics Lead
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Stripe builds the most powerful and flexible tools for running an internet business. We handle hundreds of billions of dollars each year and enable millions of users around the world to scale faster and more efficiently by building their businesses on Stripe. To further this important mission, Stripe is building a world class Internal Audit (IA) team. Our IA mission is to make the business better as it grows. We are consumed with the goal of being agile with the business, powered by technology and an accelerator to the speed of controls integration and compliance adoption.

About the team

Our IA team is responsible for providing objective feedback and insights across the company in relation to the design and effectiveness of Stripe’s business processes, its compliance with laws and regulations and its risk management framework. Unique in our purpose is a cross-functional mandate that invites viewing through a wide lens and collaborating across the business. To enable this engagement, we must build and scale in a rapid-growth, high-volume environment. This is a unique opportunity to join a growing Data Analytics team within audit and work on providing data driven insights across the IA lifecycle. The DA Lead will support Data Analytics and audit fieldwork in execution of the approved Global Audit Plan. They will help develop embedded audit analytics as part of audit planning, fieldwork, and reporting through the execution of data analytics test steps. The DA Lead will also help drive the usage of AI to help drive more efficient and effective audits and will be a key member of the IA team who will help us elevate the ambitions of Stripe.

This position can be based in Toronto, New York, or San Francisco.

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

  • Complete data analytics as part of audit engagements in collaboration with the IA team.
  • Drive the use of AI across the audit team and leverage it in audit engagements
  • Participate in audit walkthroughs and develop work programs for the in scope areas
  • Lead DA brainstorming sessions with the audit team to discuss best use of data analytics techniques in audit planning and fieldwork
  • Assist with substantive testing of audit findings during reporting
  • Document the data analytics and audit tests in work papers.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5-10 years of professional experience working in audit data analytics
  • Expertise with SQL, schema and ETL design, and data pipeline development/maintenance (e.g., Airflow).
  • Familiarity with scripting/programming for data mining and modeling (R, Python) and ETL development (Python).
  • Experience with and knowledge of machine learning techniques.
  • Experience with reporting and visualization platforms (e.g., Tableau).
  • Exquisite attention to detail.
  • A passion for building unreasonably good products and for driving defining impact.
  • Versatility and willingness to learn new technologies on the job.
  • High tolerance for rapid change and ability to navigate ambiguity.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to simplify and share succinctly.
  • Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience working with basic git command

Preferred qualifications

  • Previous experience in a high volume transactional payment environment
  • Passionate about audit and data

  • Provide technical accounting oversight for stock-based compensation and complex commission structures, ensuring accurate recording and compliance.
  • Own payroll accounting for equity compensation programs including RSUs, stock options, and ESPP, ensuring accurate recording, tax withholding treatment, and reconciliation between equity, payroll, and the intercompany general ledger.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external payroll accounting audits. Champion compliance with internal controls (SOX), US GAAP, and multi-jurisdictional payroll tax regulations.
  • Partner with our legal team, external consultants, and banking partners to establish new subsidiaries. Collaborate with Corporate Tax and Technical Accounting to set up accounting processes for new global locations.

  • Drive AI and automation adoption across payroll accounting, including AI-assisted reconciliation between payroll registers and the GL, automated variance detection, and leveraging the Databricks platform to streamline data flow across payroll, equity, and financial systems
  • Hire, train, mentor, and manage a team of payroll accountants, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and high performance.

What we look for:

  • BA, BS Degree with a focus in Economics, Business Administration, Accounting, or Finance
  • 12+ years progressive accounting experience, with at least 5+ years specifically in payroll accounting and 2+ years in a supervisory/management role within a US multinational framework
  • Chartered Accountant (CA) or CPA equivalent certification is required. CPP is strongly preferred.

  • Proven track record driving automation and AI adoption in payroll or accounting operations, with hands-on experience implementing tools that reduce manual work and improve accuracy.
  • Deep understanding of US GAAP, multi-jurisdiction tax laws, and SOX compliance. Experience with cloud-based systems (e.g., SAP, Workday, Payslip) is required

You will be responsible for driving organization, transformation, innovation and operational efficiency at scale, as well as managing key programs across global Finance teams within the Controllership organization and with our cross-functional stakeholders. You will interface with leadership to ensure transparency and visibility into our programs and projects.

You will partner with teams across the Controllership, including Order to Revenue (Revenue Operations, Billing, Revenue Accounting, Revenue Assurance), Accounting, Payroll, Tax, Treasury, and Commissions, and collaborate with cross-functional teams such as IT, Engineering, Go-to-Market, FP&A, Pricing, Sales Operations, and our Internal Audit team. The Operations team drives country-level growth initiatives that align Coinbase Bermuda's business plans to our global strategy.   • Partner with internal and external stakeholders, including banking partners, regulators, and cross-functional teams (Risk, Legal, Compliance, Security, Finance, Product, CX), to project-manage critical operations and risk initiatives.
  • Support first line of defense operations across key areas, including launch assessments and approvals, internal audits, regulatory examinations, and supervisory touchpoints.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in financial services with demonstrated oversight of operations strategy, outsourcing, and vendor management within a regulated environment.
  • Proven experience within a regulated financial institution or investment business, with a focus on trade supervision across crypto, equities, or derivatives.
  • Track record of developing and improving operational processes, producing regulator-ready documentation, and managing cross-functional delivery with senior stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with operational resilience frameworks, incident management, and business continuity planning in a financial services context.
